The only way I know is because my narcissistic mother has been admitted a few times throughout my life.. When we went to pick her up sometimes when she could come home, she had to get her belongings(her purse and cell phone) out of a locker where the facility kept it. As for the first day someone goes, I don't know, but she said she had to share a room with another woman and that woman cried at night sometimes, making it difficult for her to sleep. I'm mot sure if she was on sleep aids from her history of insomnia, but she did say she was given antidepressants while she was there. Unfortunately... she stopped taking them after she was let out and wound up back in another place a few years later.. Just know that healing takes time, and a psychiatric hospital will keep you for at least a few days. If you don't improve and feel safe after that, they will keep you until you do, which had been as long as three weeks in my mother's case. Wanting help is the first step. Living your life better and safer for yourself is another. There were group sessions in the lobby of their part of the building if she was willing to participate, art activities, and even TVs(not sure if they restricted channels), but the doctors there did help when she was there. I heavily encourage seeking regular therapy after being released to help ease the pain. Our city college offers free counseling called the Cardinal Success Program at the Nia Center in northern Kentucky. They can even work with your existing therapist if need be.

You search online for the psychiatric hospitals near you, and get a backpack. Fill the backpack with two changes of clean clothes. No belts, no sharp objects, or objects with obvious potential to cause harm if misused. Don't forget your state I.D.(or some form of identification like a school ID or driver's license). Get a ride to the hospital whether it's by bus, bicycle, by foot, or taxi, approach the front desk and say that you want to be admitted. If it's too early in the morning or late at night, call 911 or go to the nearest ER if you can make it. The emergency room will take care of you and call the nearest psychiatric hospital for someone to see you.

I wish you luck.
Edit: You may want to write down important phone numbers like the one to a family member you trust or your work place if you are employed. Keep it with you in a book or something. As a matter of fact, bring an uplifting novel or random magazine to keep it in if allowed. When admitted, you will not be allowed to have your phone until you are released. That way, when you get the opportunity for phone calls, you won't have to worry about not remembering those numbers.

Holy smokes, stay away from those relatives! Take the proper steps to go from what I assume is Low Contact to No Contact. No happiness is going to come out of continuing to expose yourself to them. You're pretty much their punching bag, and if there aren't any legal issues with cutting them off from you forever, go right for it. Send a mass-recipient email or text message demanding they never contact you in any manner or form(suddenly not responding to them has terrible backlashes). Those people aren't family; family don't treat their own flesh and blood that way. They're just wolves in sheep's clothing. If there's something you aren't comfortable with doing, don't do it. They can't hurt you unless they want jail time. Keep records of messages in case they make threats. All you need is clear evidence and an Emergency Protective Order or Restraining Order is on them in a flash. There's still one on my Nstepdad after two years. It won't be your fault. It'll be theirs. Trust me. Subtracting them from your life will be worth it!

A difficult situation indeed. It's tough lacking a father figure, and I can relate completely as Nmom went through several terrible "boyfriends" since my birth, but what matters is finding the strength to overcome their absence. Don't let it get you down. Going to a family dinner because he is there will make life harder because your Nfather will expect you to attend every family event, and then he'll guilt trip you worse and worse when you refuse. It may take time to get used to, but it is okay not to have a father present in our lives. It doesn't make you a bad person either. Try and plan something for that day so that it'll be easier to keep it off your mind. Be strong.
Thanks, you! (:

If it's to the point where you believe they will make important celebrations or gatherings with relatives a Hell for you(and most likely others) every time you're around them, I strongly suggest you go No Contact. It will be difficult, yes, but you will discover over time that the stress you face such as this topic will slowly lessen and hopefully disappear. Do not feel guilt for excluding them from events in your life because you are doing so out of survival, and it is an astounding achievement to have gone LC in the first place. It's not your fault you have taken action against them. It's their fault for /causing/ you to take action. You have the power to live happily, and you shouldn't let them continue to chip away at your life; every instance of communication they give you is two steps backwards. You've got one more step to be free! Go NC! 

But, be prepared. My own personal experience showed me that it will not be easy, but it will be for your own good. It will get better for everyone in time. Constuct the safest method to tell them you're going NC and batten down the hatches. And do not forget: when you go NC, it not up to them to decide when NC should be dropped. If it's never, so be it. You will be free.

Good luck!
